source.title: Signed-Permutation Coordinate Transport for RMSNorm Transformers

record.tranche_reason: The paper argues that coordinate-indexed interpretability results need to be qualified by an explicit gauge, and reports gauge audits showing raw coordinate names can change while mapped objects recover. It does not measure the semantic job counts or explanation-prediction accuracy in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: Table 8's own gauge-audit outcomes for coordinate-indexed interpretability artifacts are recorded below. The text does not test neuron-pole job counts, the InceptionV1 cat-and-car example, neuron-based attribution-graph sufficiency, or explanation scores on held-out activating examples. Other gauge, steering, SAE, merging, and optimizer results do not measure those claim versions.
record.test_reason: The paper studies gauge symmetry (signed permutations) of residual-stream coordinates in RMSNorm/LayerNorm transformers and audits whether coordinate names survive exact function-preserving reparameterizations. It never measures how many neurons have one main job, whether explanations predict firing, or neuron-based attribution-graph sufficiency. It neither tests nor relies on the neurons-are-clean finding. Its point that neuron indices are gauge-relative bears on coordinate identity, not on per-neuron semantic monosemanticity, which is invariant under relabeling. So T6. The record's 'discusses/T5' overstates the link: the paper makes no argument that any version is wrong.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors also stress that RMSNorm models have signed-permutation gauge B_d, not just permutation gauge S_d. They show that permutation-only alignment breaks SAE, steering and LoRA transfer, merging and optimizer-state transport. They also show that coordinate names are well-posed only once B_d is named.
record.recipe_differences: The study performs exact gauge-equivariance audits of coordinate-indexed artifacts; it does not reproduce the neuron-explanation or Qwen3 pole-audit methods in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper distinguishes raw coordinates from gauge-mapped coordinates; the reported audits use exact function-preserving reparameterizations.

fits_no_version.finding: Under exact function-preserving gauges, raw neuron/coordinate indices of knowledge neurons, steering vectors and attribution sets move (0/10 overlap), while gauge-mapped indices recover 10/10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Index-level neuron claims are reproducible across checkpoints only relative to an explicit coordinate gauge (signed permutations for RMSNorm).

record.problems: The reported interpretability audits address coordinate identity, not the semantic quality or predictive accuracy of neuron explanations. The Table 8 entries do not state uncertainty estimates, and some do not identify a model.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows were omitted from the claim-relevant Table 8 audit results. Other reported experiments concern gauge recovery, steering transfer, SAE reconstruction, merging, or optimizer-state transport and do not test the listed claim versions.

job shares across other dense/MoE models and scale
InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron; recursive generalization vs superposition
neuron-based attribution graphs without a replacement model
explanations from activating examples vs prediction of firing

record.verdict_notes: Relation changed to cites_only and tranche to T6. The paper makes no claim about neuron monosemanticity rates or explanation quality. Gauge relabeling leaves each neuron's function unchanged, so it cannot affect V1–V7.

versions.untested_parts: The Qwen3-32B pole shares and whether poles have one or two semantic jobs.
Semantic job shares across models, architectures, or scale.
The InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron and recursive generalization versus superposition.
Interpretability-rate estimates for vision models and whether architecture or tools change those rates.
Whether attribution graphs made from a large model's own neurons explain behavior without a replacement model or reconstruction error.
Whether explanations fit activating examples but fail to predict firing on other inputs.
Automated explanation scores from simulating activations on new text.

rows.subject: BERT-base knowledge neurons
rows.operation_detail: Applied an exact function-preserving gauge and compared raw and gauge-mapped knowledge-neuron identities.
rows.measure: Recovery of the two named neurons
rows.locator: Table 8, Gauge audits for coordinate-indexed artifacts
rows.note: The audit is about coordinate identity, not whether either neuron has one main semantic job.
rows.check: Measures index recovery under an exact gauge, not neuron semantic jobs. Also, BERT knowledge neurons are FFN hidden units, governed by the FFN permutation symmetry (Corollary E.2), not the residual gauge.

rows.subject: Llama-2 refusal direction
rows.operation_detail: Applied an exact function-preserving gauge and compared raw top-coordinate names with gauge-recovered coordinates.
rows.locator: Table 8, Gauge audits for coordinate-indexed artifacts
rows.note: The table also reports the refusal ablation invariant check as 100% → 15%; that is not a neuron-job or explanation-accuracy result.
rows.check: Coordinate-identity audit of a refusal direction; no bearing on any version. The 100%→15% figure is a refusal-ablation behaviour check.

rows.subject: CAA steering vectors
rows.operation_detail: Applied an exact function-preserving gauge and compared raw top-coordinate summaries and the mapped steering effect.
rows.locator: Table 8, Gauge audits for coordinate-indexed artifacts
rows.note: The table says the mapped effect is preserved; it reports effect error <10^-4 and CKA=1. The model is not identified in this table.
rows.check: Model not stated in Table 8. Appendix I/H suggest CAA sycophancy vectors (TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat in Table 16). Not about neuron explanations.

rows.subject: Gradient×activation attribution
rows.operation_detail: Applied an exact function-preserving gauge and compared raw and mapped top attribution indices.
rows.locator: Table 8, Gauge audits for coordinate-indexed artifacts
rows.note: This concerns index recovery under a gauge, not attribution-graph sufficiency or explanation accuracy.
rows.check: Index recovery for gradient×activation attribution, not attribution-graph sufficiency (V5).
